outcome: Pathways related to neurodevelopment and synaptic function
Heritability to human intelligence, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder
cohort: Female inbred Genetic Absence Epilepsy Rats from Strasbourg and non-epileptic control rats were fed standard chow or valproate mixed in chow for two weeks prior to conception and throughout pregnancy.
finding: Gestational VPA exposure via chronic maternal oral dosing was associated with substantial drug-induced differential gene expression and dysregulated splicing in pup brains, with downregulated genes significantly enriched for neurodevelopment and synaptic function pathways, and for heritability to human intelligence, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.
gest_age: Foetuses extracted on gestational Day 21 (1 day prior to birth)
